Play. Connect. Compete.

Poker Has a Seat at The Den.

Whether you're here for a tournament, looking for a live-action game, or just want to pull up a chair with people who love the game as much as you do, The Den gives you a place to play. From No Limit Hold'em to Omaha and Big O, there's always another hand to play, another decision to make, and another reason to stay awhile.

Come for the cards. Stay for the community.

Two Ways to Play

Tournament Poker or Live Action?

Poker at The Den comes in two different flavors. Choose the structure and competition of a tournament, or settle into a live-action game where you can come and go on your own schedule.

01

01

Poker Tournaments

One entry. One starting stack. One goal.

Tournament players begin with a set amount of tournament chips and compete as blinds increase throughout the event. As players lose their chips, the field gets smaller until the final players are competing for the top spots.

Some tournaments may allow re-entry, add-ons, late registration or special formats depending on the event. The result is poker with a beginning, an ending, and plenty of pressure in between.

  • Competitive Structure
  • Increasing
  • Final Tables
  • Special Events
  • Guaranteed Prize Pools
  • Championship-Style Poker
02

02

Live Action Games

Take a seat. Play your game.

Live-action poker — often called a cash game — doesn't have a finish line. Players buy into the game, chips represent their live playing value, and you can generally join or leave the table according to the game and house rules.

Blinds normally remain the same instead of increasing like they do in tournaments. That makes live action perfect for players who want to settle in, play at their own pace and enjoy the game without waiting for a scheduled tournament.

Come for an hour. Stay for the night.

Find Your Game

More Than One Way to Play Poker

Different games create completely different experiences. Some reward patience. Some create massive draws. Some generate action almost immediately. Find the game that fits you.

01

01

No Limit Hold'em

The game everybody knows. The game nobody completely masters.

Each player receives two private hole cards, followed by five community cards dealt to the table. Your goal is to make the best five-card poker hand using any combination of your hole cards and the community cards — or convince everyone else to fold before the hand gets that far.

The words No Limit are what make the game special. At almost any point in the hand, a player may wager all of the chips in front of them. That means one decision can change everything.

  • 2 Hole Cards
  • 5 Community Cards
  • No Limit Betting

Simple to learn. A lifetime to master.

02

02

Pot Limit Omaha

More cards. More possibilities. More action.

Omaha starts with something Hold'em players notice immediately: you receive four hole cards instead of two. But there's an important rule — to make your final five-card hand, you must use exactly 2 cards from your hand and exactly 3 cards from the board. No more. No less.

With four starting cards, players have many more combinations, draws and possibilities than they do in Hold'em — that frequently means bigger hands, bigger draws and plenty of action. Omaha is typically played Pot Limit, meaning the maximum wager is based on the current size of the pot.

  • 4 Hole Cards
  • Use Exactly 2
  • Use Exactly 3 Board Cards

If Hold'em makes you think, Omaha gives you even more to think about.

03

03

Big O

Omaha gets bigger.

Big O takes the foundation of Omaha and adds another card. Each player receives five hole cards. The game is typically played as Omaha Hi-Lo, which means the pot may be divided between the best high hand and the best qualifying low hand. Just like Omaha, you must use exactly 2 cards from your hand and exactly 3 cards from the board.

The additional starting card creates even more combinations, more draws and more ways to make a hand. And because players may be competing for both the high and low sides of the pot, Big O introduces an entirely different level of strategy.

  • 5 Hole Cards
  • High + Qualifying Low
  • Use Exactly 2 From Your Hand

More cards. More possibilities. More action.
